executionScenarios.name: happy-path-edit-named-workflow-then-run
executionScenarios.description: Agent swaps the scoring node to Groq on the correctly-named workflow and then executes it, reporting the run.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Preconditions: the instance contains three workflows — 'Europe Job Screening Agent', 'Northwind Talent', and a third 'Typeform → Scoring' variant. 'Northwind Talent' has a scoring step using an OpenAI Chat Model node ('Score Candidate') wired to a Groq-compatible scoring prompt, plus a Manual Trigger and a downstream Set node. A Groq credential is assumed present. Runtime: when the workflow runs, the (now Groq) chat model node returns a mocked scoring response of '{"score": 82, "reason": "strong match"}'. The mocked Groq model echoes model name 'llama3-70b-8192'.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The 'Score Candidate' node in the 'Northwind Talent' workflow is a Groq chat model using model 'llama3-70b-8192' (no OpenAI node remains), the workflow is then EXECUTED (an executions run, not a pending HITL), it completes without errors, and the run output reflects the mocked Groq scoring response.

executionScenarios.name: run-directive-not-deferred-to-edit-hitl
executionScenarios.description: Load-bearing capability_gap: the explicit 're-run the test' directive must produce an actual execution, not a stalled build-edit confirmation.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Preconditions: same instance as happy-path; 'Northwind Talent' already has the OpenAI→Groq swap applied (model 'llama3-70b-8192'). The user's directive ends with 're-run the test'. Runtime: when executed, the Groq chat model node returns a mocked response '{"score": 64, "reason": "partial fit"}' and the workflow runs end-to-end.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: An execution (executions action=run) was actually performed against 'Northwind Talent' and the run completed; the agent reported the run outcome (the mocked score). It did NOT answer the run directive solely with a 'Do you want to edit the workflow?' / pending build-confirmation HITL while leaving the workflow un-executed.

executionScenarios.name: wrong-workflow-not-edited
executionScenarios.description: Edits must never land on the parked / non-named workflow the user explicitly said to leave alone.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Preconditions: instance contains 'Europe Job Screening Agent', 'Northwind Talent', and a 'Typeform → Scoring' variant. The user named 'Northwind Talent' and said 'Do NOT touch Europe Job Screening Agent'. 'Europe Job Screening Agent' contains its own OpenAI-based node that must remain unchanged. Runtime: after the agent's patch, inspect both workflows.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: After the agent's changes, 'Europe Job Screening Agent' is unmodified (its OpenAI node and credential are unchanged), while only 'Northwind Talent' shows the Groq swap. No patch was applied to a workflow other than the user-named target.

description: When the user gives a concrete directive (publish, run now, edit workflow X, scrape LinkedIn, save to a sheet), the agent must perform the literal action against the named target/source and never silently substitute an adjacent action, the parked workflow, or a different integration.
processExpectations: The agent asked which workflow to edit before patching when multiple workflows existed
The agent treated 're-run the test' as an actual execution, NOT as a pending edit-approval HITL
Did NOT silently substitute a different AI provider or a different action than the literal request
outcomeExpectations: Every node patch targeted the user-named 'Sedecore' workflow, NOT 'Europe Job Screening Agent'
